target.name: American Housing Corporation
target.founder: Bobby Fijan, Riley Meik, Harris Rothaermel, William Davis

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Pre-Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $3M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
American Housing Corporation is a Pre-Seed stage company in Housing & Construction founded by Bobby Fijan, Riley Meik, Harris Rothaermel, and William Davis. The company has raised approximately $2.7M to date. Notably, no public or private comparables were identified in the sector, limiting triangulation to stage-based progression analysis.

The valuation assessment relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x multiplier to the $3M total-raised proxy, standard for Pre-Seed to next-stage advancement. This method yields an implied valuation of $7M. The absence of peer comps—both public and private—constrains our ability to validate this estimate against transaction multiples or traded valuations typical in housing and construction.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M to $8M (median $7M), with the range reflecting ±15% variance around the stage-based estimate. The principal uncertainty is the lack of comparable company data; this valuation should be treated as preliminary pending access to relevant private or public peer sets, product-market validation metrics, or articulation of the company's specific technical or operational differentiation within housing and construction. Additional diligence on capital efficiency, customer traction, and competitive positioning is necessary before confidence in this range can be elevated.
